title: Retroperitoneal Sarcoma Surgery: A Step-by-Step Technical Analysis
summary:
Retroperitoneal sarcomas (RPS) are rare malignant tumors that develop in the back of the abdominal cavity. The course of the disease depends, among other factors, on the exact type and aggressiveness of the tumor and whether it can be completely removed.

Surgery is currently the only treatment that may offer a chance of long-term cure. The tumor is often removed together with directly adjacent tissue to reduce the risk of it returning. Most procedures are performed through an open abdominal incision. In selected cases, minimally invasive or robot-assisted surgery may also be possible. However, these techniques are not yet routinely used.

The aim of this study is to systematically examine and improve the surgical treatment of retroperitoneal sarcomas. Information about the patient, the tumor, the operation, and the course of recovery will be collected. Participation in the study will not change the treatment itself.

For the analysis, each operation will be divided into seven stages: patient positioning; the surgical incision or placement of surgical instruments; exposure and removal of the tumor; removal of the resected tissue from the body; reconstruction of affected structures; placement of drains and wound closure; and the instruments used. Each stage will then be evaluated by the operating surgeon and the surgical assistant. The evaluation will examine how the procedure is normally performed, whether any adjustments were necessary, what benefits or difficulties occurred, and what can be learned for future operations.

The study will also assess blood loss, duration of surgery, possible complications, postoperative pain, mobilization after surgery, recovery, and mortality within 30 and 90 days. Minimally invasive or robot-assisted procedures may also be video-recorded and analyzed.

A total of 40 patients will be enrolled at one study center. In addition to patients with retroperitoneal sarcoma, patients with other tumors located in the back of the abdominal cavity may also participate if the location and surgical approach are comparable. This may be the case, for example, if the exact type of tumor could not be clearly determined before surgery.

The study is intended to help ensure the quality of these procedures and support the development of structured recommendations for the surgical treatment of these rare tumors. Both the technical feasibility of the procedure and the oncological safety of tumor removal will be considered.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
-Presence of a retroperitoneal sarcoma or retroperitoneal tumor
-Performing elective tumor resection
-Written informed consent
Exclusion criteria:
Missing informed consent
